home.gettingStartedSub: Step-by-step walkthrough for your first frame extraction.

gettingStartedSteps.title: Step 1: Prepare Your Video
gettingStartedSteps.content: Ensure your video is in a supported format (MP4 H.264 is most compatible). For best results, use H.264 encoded MP4 files. If you have HEVC/H.265, ProRes, or AV1 files, transcode them first using HandBrake (free) to MP4 H.264 for guaranteed browser compatibility.

gettingStartedSteps.title: Step 2: Load the Video
gettingStartedSteps.content: Drag and drop your video file onto the upload zone, or click "Choose File" to browse. The tool loads the video entirely in your browser memory — no upload progress bar, no server connection. Large files (2+ GB) may take a few seconds to decode the first frame.

gettingStartedSteps.title: Step 3: Choose Extraction Mode
gettingStartedSteps.content: Select your preferred extraction method: (a) Exact Timestamp — enter HH:MM:SS.mmm or use frame-step buttons for single-frame precision; (b) Custom FPS — choose from presets (1, 5, 10, 12, 15, 24, 25, 30, 60) or use the slider for any value 1–60; (c) Every Frame — extracts at native video frame rate for complete sequences.

gettingStartedSteps.title: Step 4: Select Output Format & Quality
gettingStartedSteps.content: Choose JPG (smallest files, universal compatibility), PNG (lossless, alpha transparency for VFX/ML), or WebP (25–35% smaller than JPG, supports transparency, modern browsers). Adjust quality slider for JPG/WebP (10–100).

gettingStartedSteps.title: Step 5: Extract & Preview
gettingStartedSteps.content: Click "Extract Frames" to begin. Progress bar shows real-time frame count. The preview grid displays thumbnails of extracted frames. You can click any thumbnail to view full-resolution, or use "Load More" for large extractions.

gettingStartedSteps.title: Step 6: Download Results
gettingStartedSteps.content: Download individual frames by clicking them, or use "Download All (ZIP)" for the complete sequence. Frames are named sequentially (frame_000001.png) for easy import into Blender, FFmpeg, Python, or labeling tools.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.sub: Everything about extracting frames from video in your browser

items.q: How do I extract frames from a video?
items.a: Upload your video, choose extraction mode (exact timestamp, custom FPS, or every frame), pick output format (JPG, PNG, WebP), and click Extract. Frames appear in a grid — download individually or as ZIP.

items.q: How many frames should I extract per second?
items.a: Depends on your goal: 1 FPS for slide capture, 5–10 FPS for motion sampling, 24–30 FPS for smooth sequences/VFX, 60 FPS for high-speed analysis. For AI datasets, 1–5 FPS is typical.

items.q: What is the difference between FPS and frame interval?
items.a: FPS = frames extracted per second of video. Interval = every N-th frame (e.g., interval 30 = 1 frame every 30 frames). This tool uses FPS for intuitive control.

items.q: Can I extract every frame from a video?
items.a: Yes. Select the highest FPS preset (60) or use 'every frame' mode on the extractor page. A 10-second 30 FPS video yields ~300 frames. Large outputs download as ZIP.

items.q: Can I extract a frame at an exact timestamp?
items.a: Yes. Use the Exact Timestamp Extractor: enter HH:MM:SS.mmm (e.g., 00:01:23.450), or scrub frame-by-frame with Previous/Next buttons. Capture at full native resolution.
PNG and WebP (lossless mode) are lossless. JPG is lossy but high quality (92%). For VFX/ML, use PNG. For web/thumbnails, WebP balances quality and size.

items.q: JPG vs PNG vs WebP for extracted video frames?
items.a: JPG: smallest, universal. PNG: lossless, alpha channel. WebP: 25–35% smaller than JPG, supports alpha, modern browser support. Choose WebP for web delivery.

items.q: How much RAM is needed for browser-based extraction?
items.a: 1080p at 24–30 FPS: 4–8 GB. 4K or high FPS: 8–16 GB. If tab crashes, lower FPS, close tabs, or split video into shorter clips.

items.q: Why does a video fail to decode?
items.a: Unsupported codec (e.g., ProRes, AV1 without hardware decode). Re-encode to MP4 H.264 with HandBrake (free) for best compatibility.
MP4 (H.264, H.265), MOV (H.264, ProRes*), WEBM (VP8, VP9, AV1*). *Depends on browser hardware support. Safari/iOS has limited H.265/AV1 support.

items.q: Can I extract frames from a 4K video?
items.a: Yes, but 4K frames consume 4× memory of 1080p. Use lower FPS (1–5) and ensure 16 GB+ RAM. Frames are downscaled to 1920 px max during preview; downloads are full resolution.

items.q: How do I create an image sequence for Blender?
items.a: Extract as PNG (lossless, alpha), name pattern frame_000001.png. In Blender: Add → Image Sequence, select folder. Set frame rate to match extraction FPS.

items.q: How do I extract frames for a computer vision dataset?
items.a: Use 1–5 FPS for classification/detection, higher for tracking. Export PNG for pixel-perfect labels. ZIP download works with labeling tools (CVAT, LabelImg, Roboflow).
